description: Defines and enforces plugin-level rules (R1-R33) governing all components in a Claude Code plugin.

evals.name: Catches a real R4 kebab-case violation
evals.prompt: Create a scratch test skill directory at C:\Dev\Repos\andres-cc-marketplace\.claude\worktrees\plugin-auditor-codex-integration\evals\plugin-rulebook\workspace\iteration-1\eval-1\with_skill\outputs\scratch-test-skill\ containing a SKILL.md with frontmatter name: 'Scratch_Test_Skill' (note: this violates R4's kebab-case requirement -- underscores and capital letters). Give it a minimal valid description and body. Then apply the plugin-rulebook skill's Compliance Check Procedure against this test skill and report which rule(s) it flags, at what severity (REQUIRED/ADVISORY), and what the correct fix would be. Do NOT delete the scratch-test-skill directory when done -- leave it for inspection.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies R4 (Naming: Kebab-Case Only, REQUIRED) as violated by 'Scratch_Test_Skill', explains the fix (rename to 'scratch-test-skill'), and does not report false positives on other rules for this minimal valid skill.

evals.name: No false positives on a clean, compliant component
evals.prompt: Apply the plugin-rulebook skill's Compliance Check Procedure against plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/scripts/validate_evidence.py (worktree: C:\Dev\Repos\andres-cc-marketplace\.claude\worktrees\plugin-auditor-codex-integration) -- this is a real, already-shipped, presumed-compliant file. Report your findings.
evals.expected_output: Reports the file as compliant (or with only pre-existing, already-known advisory items if any) -- does not invent a false REQUIRED violation against a real, shipped file.

evals.name: R27 respects an R33-registered prefix on a command filename
evals.prompt: A plugin named 'git-kit' has a registered R33 prefix of 'git' in marketplace-inventory.json, status 'active'. It has a command file at commands/git-commit.md (frontmatter name 'git-commit', a minimal valid description and body). Apply the plugin-rulebook skill's R27 (Component Naming: Grammatical Form) check to this command file, given the plugin's registered prefix. Report whether R27 flags it, and why.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT flag 'git-commit.md' under R27 -- correctly strips the registered 'git-' prefix first, then recognizes 'commit' as a verb, so the command is verb-first per the documented convention. Explicitly reasons about the prefix-stripping step, not just the full basename.

evals.name: R27 still checks the full basename when no prefix is registered
evals.prompt: A plugin named 'misc-kit' has no registered R33 prefix (its marketplace-inventory.json record has "prefix": null and no 'domain_prefix'). It has a command file at commands/config-settings.md (frontmatter name 'config-settings', a minimal valid description and body -- 'config' is a noun, not a verb). Apply the plugin-rulebook skill's R27 (Component Naming: Grammatical Form) check to this command file. Report whether R27 flags it, and why.
evals.expected_output: DOES flag 'config-settings.md' under R27 (ADVISORY) -- since no prefix is registered, the full basename is checked as-is, and 'config' is not a recognizable verb.

evals.name: R33 treats an explicit prefix null as a deliberate opt-out
evals.prompt: A plugin named 'example-kit' has a marketplace-inventory.json record with "prefix": null and no "domain_prefix" key at all (a deliberate, recorded opt-out). It has a file at scripts/helper.sh (no plugin prefix in its basename). Apply the plugin-rulebook skill's R33 (Component-File Naming: Plugin Prefix Required) check to this plugin. Report whether R33 raises any finding for scripts/helper.sh or for the inventory record, and why.
evals.expected_output: R33 raises NO finding: an explicit prefix null with no domain_prefix is a deliberate opt-out, so the rule is inert for this plugin (helper.sh is not flagged), and the record itself is not a violation because the prefix key is present.

evals.name: R33 still enforces a registered prefix (pdk) on a mis-prefixed file
evals.prompt: A plugin named 'plugin-devkit', status 'active', has a marketplace-inventory.json record with prefix 'pdk' and domain_prefix 'plugindevkit'. Its root scripts/ directory contains: scripts/pdk-lib.sh, scripts/helper-utils.sh, scripts/inventory_common/pdk_models.py, and scripts/inventory_common/__init__.py. Apply the plugin-rulebook skill's R33 check. Give a verdict per file (pass, exempt, or flagged) with the reason.
evals.expected_output: Only scripts/helper-utils.sh is flagged (basename starts with neither 'pdk-' nor 'plugindevkit-'). pdk-lib.sh passes (pdk- prefix); pdk_models.py passes (.py snake_case form pdk_); inventory_common/__init__.py is exempt (a Python package's __init__.py under the plugin-root scripts/).

evals.name: R33 does not silently treat an omitted prefix key as inert
evals.prompt: A plugin named 'legacy-kit', status 'active', has a marketplace-inventory.json record with id, name, source and status fields but NO 'prefix' key at all (the key is absent, which is different from an explicit null). It has a file at scripts/legacy-tool.sh. According to the plugin-rulebook skill's R33 as documented, how should this record be treated? Report whether it is a finding, what kind, and what the fix is.
evals.expected_output: Reports the record as non-compliant: R33 states every plugin's inventory record must carry a prefix key, and an explicit null (with no domain_prefix) is the only sanctioned opt-out. An absent key is NOT silently treated as inert or as an opt-out; the fix is to add the key (a curated prefix, or an explicit null if opting out).

evals.name: R34 flags an escaping path and a dead link but not a legitimate plugin-root pointer
evals.prompt: Read plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/SKILL.md and plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/references/reference-integrity.md (read these files directly; do not rely on any other copy of the skill). A newly-created skill 'demo-skill' in plugin 'example-kit' (a plugin NOT listed in scripts_mirrors) has a SKILL.md with three relative references: (1) a markdown link to '../../references/shared-contract.md', which exists at the plugin root; (2) a markdown link to '../../docs/design-notes.md', which exists at the plugin root; (3) a markdown link to 'references/missing-guide.md', which does not exist anywhere. Using the plugin-rulebook skill's R34 as documented in those files, report each of the three: finding or not, the severity, and the fix.
evals.expected_output: (1) is NOT a finding: '..' alone is not a violation, and it lands in the plugin-root references/ folder, which the .claude/ mirror carries. (2) is a Critical finding: it leaves the skill folder and lands in docs/, which is not a mirrored plugin-root folder; fix by moving the shared file into plugin-root references/ or assets/. (3) is a Critical finding: a markdown link that resolves to nothing; fix by correcting the path or creating the file.

evals.name: R35 requires Reference Guide only when a references directory exists, and leaves Testing & Validation to R29
evals.prompt: Read plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/SKILL.md and plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/references/standard-sections.md (read these files directly; do not rely on any other copy of the skill). A newly-created skill has a SKILL.md with these ## headings only: Quick Start, When to Use This Skill, Testing & Validation. It has no references/ directory. Using the plugin-rulebook skill's R35 as documented in those files, report which required sections are missing, whether the missing Reference Guide or the 'When to Use This Skill' wording is a problem, and what happens with Testing & Validation.
evals.expected_output: Reports '## When NOT to Use' as the one missing required section. 'When to Use This Skill' satisfies '## When to Use' because headings are matched by substance, not exact wording. '## Reference Guide' is not required because the skill has no references/ directory. Testing & Validation is not checked by R35 at all; R29 owns it, so a missing or present heading is never reported twice.

evals.name: R36 reports only overlapping one-way exclusions, not pure delegation
evals.prompt: Read plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/SKILL.md and plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/references/reciprocal-exclusions.md (read these files directly; do not rely on any other copy of the skill). A newly-created skill 'deep-review' has a '## When NOT to Use' section containing two lines: (a) 'Reviewing a single skill's structure -> use skill-quick-check instead', and (b) 'Saving the reviewed changes to version control -> use save-changes instead'. Neither 'skill-quick-check' (another review skill that covers a single skill's structure; a request to review one skill could plausibly match either) nor 'save-changes' (a helper that records changes to version control) names 'deep-review' anywhere in its When NOT to Use or description. Using the plugin-rulebook skill's R36 as documented in those files, report for (a) and (b): finding or not, severity, and what the fix would be.
evals.expected_output: (a) is an ADVISORY finding reported against skill-quick-check: the two review skills overlap, so a request could match either, and skill-quick-check should name deep-review back with its own half of the distinguishing criterion. (b) is NOT a finding: pointing at save-changes is pure delegation to a differently-scoped helper whose domain would never attract review requests. R36 is ADVISORY, never blocking, and the report states the overlap it judged.

evals.name: R37 does not exempt a hook script because shell is set to bash
evals.prompt: Read plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/SKILL.md and plugins/plugin-devkit/skills/plugin-rulebook/references/executable-bit.md (read these files directly; do not rely on any other copy of the skill). A newly-created plugin ships a hook whose hooks.json command is the bare path "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/guard.sh" with "shell": "bash" set. `git ls-files -s` shows guard.sh at mode 100644, while `ls -l` on the author's machine shows it executable. The same plugin's skill also has `allowed-tools: Bash(python:*)` and runs scripts/tool.py through it; `git ls-files -s` shows tool.py at mode 100644. Using the plugin-rulebook skill's R37 as documented in those files, report for guard.sh and for tool.py: finding or not, severity, which mode source counts, and the fix.
evals.expected_output: guard.sh is a REQUIRED finding: it is run directly by a bare-path hook command, its committed mode is 100644, and the 'shell: bash' setting does NOT exempt it because a shell running a non-executable path directly fails with Permission denied. The committed mode from `git ls-files -s` counts, not the on-disk `ls -l` bit. Fix: git update-index --chmod=+x (and chmod +x) in every mirrored copy. tool.py is NOT a finding: it is run through the python interpreter grant, which is not a direct invocation.
